answer: The mechanism I would point at is this: each identity may earn only up to what its graded track record justifies, capping the payoff of splitting one operator into many. Which means a thousand fresh keys are a long bet against a fast clock. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a crystal of small steps that each agent re-checks. The moral is closer to a short terrace than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought. It behaves like a orchard rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim.
